cards.prompt: After a big storm, a picture spreads everywhere: a shark swimming down a flooded street, past a bus stop. Your friend sends it: "OMG look at this!!" Staring at it won't tell you if it's real. But many search tools let you search with a picture itself.

choices.text: Share it to your group: everyone needs to see this
choices.consequence: If it's fake, you've just spread it further. Check first.

choices.text: Search with the picture to see where it first appeared
choices.consequence: The same shark picture turns up years ago, after a different storm, in another country, already marked as edited.

choices.text: Zoom in and look for six fingers or jumbled signs
choices.consequence: You find nothing odd, but that proves nothing. The fastest check is where it came from.

steps.text: It's an old edited picture. What now?

choices.text: Tell your friend kindly where it really came from
choices.consequence: Nice: they won't share it now, and nobody felt silly.

choices.text: Say nothing: it's their problem, not yours
choices.consequence: They might share it further. A kind word now stops it spreading.

cards.hint: Think about what you can find out from outside the picture, instead of from staring at it.
cards.explanation: **Search for where it first appeared**: old pictures often come back after every storm. Staring for give-aways can't prove a picture is real. And be kind: anyone can be fooled.

cards.title: How to check a picture
cards.body:
- **Find where it first appeared**: search with the picture itself.
- **Look for trusted news** showing it, ideally from other angles.
- **Check the account**: is it new? Lots of shocking posts?
- **Check the details**: do the place, weather and date fit?

Likes, sharpness and who sent it prove nothing. If **you** post an AI picture, say it's AI.

cards.prompt:
Some AI tools add a [[watermark]]: a visible mark, or hidden information inside the file, saying AI made it. Some apps add an AI label too.

A picture has no AI label and no watermark. What does that tell you?

options.text: The app checked it and found it was a real photo
options.nudge: Apps don't check every picture. Could a mark go missing, or never be added?

options.text: It was made by AI, and the label was hidden on purpose
options.nudge: That's possible, but you can't tell from a missing label. What does "no label" really prove?

options.text: Not much: a label may have been removed, or never added
It's a real photo, because AI pictures always have a label
options.nudge: Many AI tools add nothing, and labels can be cropped off. What does that mean?

cards.hint: Could a visible mark be cut off? Could hidden information get lost when someone takes a screenshot? Does every tool add one?
cards.explanation: Visible marks get cropped off, a screenshot can throw away hidden information saved with the file, and many tools add nothing. So an AI label is good evidence when it's there, but **no label proves nothing**.

cards.prompt: Does each one **help** you tell if a picture is real, or is it a **myth**?

items.label: A label saying AI made it
It has lots of likes and shares
A friend you trust sent it

cards.hint: Which ones tell you where the picture came from, and which only tell you how popular or nice it looks?
cards.nudge: A friend can be fooled too, and fakes spread fast and look sharp. Which ones are about the picture's real origin?
cards.explanation: Where it **first appeared**, **trusted news**, and an **AI label** are real evidence. Likes, a trusted friend sending it, sharpness, and a missing label are **myths**: fakes get likes, friends get fooled, AI pictures are sharp, and labels go missing.

cards.prompt: Which is the **strongest** sign that a dramatic picture is real?

options.text: It's been shared over a million times today
options.nudge: Fakes spread fast, often faster than the truth. What would really show it happened?

options.text: It's very high quality, with tiny details everywhere
options.nudge: AI pictures can be very detailed. What would show it really happened?

options.text: Several trusted news sites show it, from different angles
There's no AI label or watermark anywhere on it
options.nudge: Labels go missing or were never added. What would be real evidence?

cards.hint: Which one is evidence from **outside** the picture itself?
cards.explanation: Several **trusted news** sources showing it from **different angles** is strong evidence: it's hard to fake many independent views of the same moment. Shares, sharpness and missing labels prove nothing.

cards.prompt: You made a funny AI picture of your dog wearing a crown, sitting on a throne.

steps.text: You're about to post it. What's the best way?

choices.text: Post it, and say it's AI only if someone asks
choices.consequence: Most people won't ask, and the picture can travel far from your post without the answer. Say it up front.

choices.text: Post it without saying anything about how it was made
choices.consequence: Most people will guess, but some won't, and it can travel far from your caption. Saying it's AI is better.

choices.text: Post it and say it was made with AI
choices.consequence: Perfect: everyone gets the joke, and nobody's fooled.

cards.hint: Look back at what to do when **you** make an AI picture.
cards.explanation: When you post an AI picture, **say it's AI**, even when it's obviously a joke. Pictures travel far from their captions, and it keeps the internet a little more honest.

cards.prompt: An hour ago you shared a picture to your group chat: snow piled high on a summer beach. Now you find it was made with AI.

choices.text: Delete your message and say nothing
choices.consequence: People have already seen it, and some may have shared it on. Deleting doesn't tell them it's fake.

choices.text: Wait and see whether anyone actually believed it
choices.consequence: By the time you find out, it may have spread further. A quick correction now is easier than chasing it later.

choices.text: Post in the chat: "Sorry, that picture was AI, not real"
choices.consequence: Good call. Everyone who saw it now knows. Then a friend says they've already sent it to their work chat.

steps.text: Your friend has already sent it to their work chat. What now?

choices.text: Kindly ask them to post the correction there too
choices.consequence: They do, and the correction follows the picture. Nobody felt silly.

choices.text: Nothing: adults in a work chat will spot it's fake
choices.consequence: Adults get fooled too, and the fake keeps travelling without its correction. One kind message could have stopped it.

cards.hint: A picture keeps travelling after you send it. How can the truth travel with it?
cards.explanation: You can't unsend a picture, but you can **send the correction after it**: tell the people who saw it, and kindly ask anyone who passed it on to do the same. Everyone gets fooled sometimes; fixing it is what counts.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- An AI label is good evidence; no label proves nothing.
- Check where it first appeared, trusted news, the account, details.
- Check before sharing, and say when **your** pictures are AI.
